events.title: 石藥爾雅
events.text: Méi Biāo’s handbook of alchemical drug names lists twenty-one aliases for mercury alone. Metals have names, but no one has tried to fix them.

events.title: 天文略論
events.text: Benjamin Hobson coins 養氣 (nourishing gas) for oxygen and 淡氣 (diluting gas) for nitrogen.

events.title: 博物新編
events.text: Hobson’s natural philosophy names hydrogen 輕氣 and speaks of 56 elements.

events.title: 六合叢談
events.text: Alexander Wylie and Lǐ Shànlán publish the first Chinese list of 64 element names.

events.title: English and Chinese Dictionary
events.text: Wilhelm Lobscheid is the first to write elements as single coined characters, 22 of them.

events.title: 格物入門
events.text: W. A. P. Martin’s Tongwen College textbook: keep old names, otherwise name by property, transliterate as a last resort. Only 12 % of his names are one character.

events.title: Letters between Fryer and Kerr
events.text: Fryer sends his element names to Kerr in Canton for comment; Kerr adopts the principles.

events.title: 化學初階
events.text: Kerr and Hé Liǎorán’s medical chemistry, the first to print one-character names systematically.

events.title: 金石識別
events.text: MacGowan and Huà Héngfāng’s mineralogy, with multi-character transliterations and imperial-taboo avoidance (波羅明 for bromine).

events.title: 化學鑑原
events.text: Xú Shòu and John Fryer set the rule: first syllable of the Western name, one character, radical for the class. Around 92 % of the 64 names are single characters.

events.title: 化學指南
events.text: Anatole Billequin’s property-based alternative (生色 chromium, 錆 cobalt) with heavy multi-part characters. It does not catch on.

events.title: Missionary Conference, Shanghai
events.text: Fryer laments the terminological chaos, then refuses to let a committee change his own terms unless they are “radically wrong”.

events.title: 化學元素修正表
events.text: The Educational Association and the Medical Missionary Association attempt a compromise list.

events.title: 亞泉雜誌
events.text: Dù Yàquán, the first Chinese author in the story, invents the 气 radical for gases with 氬 argon, and proposes 鈹 鐠 鐿 銩 釓.

events.title: 化學語彙
events.text: The Qing Ministry of Education issues a chemical vocabulary that keeps most of the Xú–Fryer characters.

events.title: 無機化學命名草案
events.text: Republican draft; 氦 replaces 氜 for helium.

events.title: 化學定說名略
events.text: Zhèng Zhènwén’s first comprehensive draft of a unified nomenclature.

events.title: 化學命名原則
events.text: Adopted 1932, published 1933: every element one character, 氫 氧 氮 氯 fixed, 矽 for silicon. The framework still in force.

events.title: Revised principles
events.text: 氡 radon, 鈮 niobium (for columbium), 釓 gadolinium.

events.title: 矽 → 硅, 鎦 → 鑥
events.text: The mainland removes two homophones; Taiwan keeps 矽 and 鎦. The two standards begin to diverge.

events.title: 化學名詞
events.text: The national terms committee finalises all elements to 109, including 鍀 鉕 砹 鈁.

events.title: Elements 101–109
events.text: After IUPAC ends the transfermium wars, Chinese names for 鑪 𨧀 𨭎 𨨏 𨭆 䥑 are published.

events.title: Elements 113, 115, 117, 118
events.text: 鉨 鏌 鿬 鿫 chosen in a public review; Unicode adds the missing characters in 2018.

meibiao.name: Méi Biāo
meibiao.role: Tang alchemist, compiler of the 石藥爾雅

hobson.name: Benjamin Hobson
hobson.role: British medical missionary in Canton and Shanghai

martin.name: W. A. P. Martin
martin.role: American missionary, head of Tongwen College

xushou.name: Xú Shòu
xushou.role: Chemist and translator; credited with the naming rules

duyaquan.name: Dù Yàquán
duyaquan.role: Editor and textbook author, Commercial Press; took his name from 氬線
